final_rationale: The verdict does not change because the Actor supplied no new admissible evidence and largely reframed the same record. That record still supports only part of the certification theory: the release passes aggregate readiness by 2.4 percentage points and had no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and general guidance supports measurement, monitoring, and documentation of limitations. But the controlling policy is narrower: certification may proceed only if current release documentation reflects current evaluation results and material segment weaknesses are disclosed or covered by approved mitigation. The admissible evidence still shows the benefits-eligibility subgroup is below threshold, and it still does not show the required current documentation artifact, approved mitigation, or signed risk acceptance. The Actor’s narrowed position is analytically cleaner, but its caveat remains an unmet compliance condition rather than a satisfied bounded exception. That keeps the claim plausible in principle yet unsupported for present certification on the available record.
remaining_concerns: No admissible evidence shows the current release documentation already reflects the current evaluation results and expressly discloses the benefits-eligibility subgroup weakness.
No approved mitigation or reviewed risk-acceptance artifact is in the record for the subgroup weakness.
The caveat the Actor proposes is not merely explanatory; it is an unresolved policy predicate for certification.
Prior approval and the informal monitoring comment remain contextual only and cannot satisfy the current-release documentation requirement.
